newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank - no need for U.S. listing.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank - no need for U.S. listing.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG said on Tuesday it saw no need to list its shares in New York as several large German corporates have done, mainly as it did not wish to apply U.S. accounting rules.
Chairman Martin Kohlhaussen said banks, as service providers, were in a different position from companies which produced goods and had more to gain from a higher profile in the U.S.
"I see no argument for a listing in New York," he told a news conference.

"We do not wish to have to issue double accounts," he said, referring to the system under which Daimler-Benz AG, for example, had last year to produce both German-standard accounts and results according to U.S. GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles).
In its annual report, Commerzbank also argued that it saw no need to report according to International Accounting Standards (IAS), as its larger rival Deutsche Bank AG has done.
German banks have come under pressure from shareholders to provide more transparent information on their accounts since German rules are considered more opaque than U.S. and international standards.
"By no means do we regard our continued application of German accounting law...as a limitation," it said.

Not until there was a definitive scheme for applying IAS would Commerzbank switch to that system, the report added, although it also said the bank had put in place an organisational framework for the alternative accounting rules.
